title: chatv1-probabilistic-stop-demux-toolcall-framing
author: Hannah Li
release_notes: Add conservative probabilistic stop-demultiplexer for v1/chat.completions streaming; improve toolcall/structured-output framing and add backward-compatible param normalization for stop/roles/logprobs.
description:
Context: Several customers reported intermittent early-termination and malformed tool responses when using v1/chat.completions streaming + function/tool calling. Root cause analysis showed racey stop detection across fragment boundaries and ambiguous stop token sequences that could be partially emitted inside tool responses. This PR introduces a conservative, probabilistic stop-demultiplexer that defers final stop resolution until a minimal lookahead and token confidence heuristics are observed, plus a set of API-surface compatibility normalizers so existing OpenAI-compatible clients see consistent behavior.

Summary of changes: consolidated into a single continuous change set to minimize rollout risk: 1) stop_demux: new probabilistic demultiplexer that maintains a small sliding automaton across stream fragments and weights stop hypotheses by partial-token logprob signatures; 2) toolcall framing: explicit pre/post toolcall sentinels added to the framed streaming envelope, preventing tool output from being interpreted as stop sequences; 3) param coalescer: input-side normalizer for v1/chat.completions that coerces stop param shapes (string|array) and merges role aliases (eg role: 'assistant'/'bot') so semantic parity with common OpenAI clients is improved; 4) logprob fallback: when logprobs are missing for partial tokens on the final fragment, we fall back to model confidence buckets instead of forcing a stop; 5) tests and docs: e2e harness scenarios that reproduce early-stop and toolcall-embedded-stop cases, and API docs note the new stable behavior and guidance for latency-sensitive callers.

Why this approach: deterministic, greedy stop detectors were causing false-positives on low-latency fragment boundaries and when tool outputs contained token patterns matching stop sequences. The probabilistic demuxer lowers false-positive rate while keeping the final observed latency within SLOs by using a short lookahead (configurable) and token confidence heuristics. Coupling that with explicit toolcall framing removes ambiguity at the envelope level, which simplifies downstream SDK logic.

Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is backward-compatible for existing v1 clients. The param coalescer runs on the server-side before any routing happens; no client changes required. The probabilistic demuxer is enabled by default for streaming endpoints because it reduces incidents observed in the field; however an opt-out flag (x-redwood-stop-mode=legacy) was added for customers that require historical behavior during a transitional window.

Operational notes & rollout: feature gated behind a gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with canary metrics tracked in the Redwood Console: stream-early-termination-rate, toolcall-framing-errors, stream-latency-95. We ran a 2-day canary on production and saw early-termination rate drop ~78% with <3ms p95 added latency on our test clusters.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-3245) - [x] Unit tests for stop_demux edge cases - [x] e2e replay tests for toolcall-embedded-stop - [x] SDK adjustment (python) to prefer new framing when present - [x] Console metrics & dashboard updates

Edge cases & open items: - Extremely low-latency (<10ms) fragment policies may still observe tighter tradeoffs; guidance in docs suggests setting max_fragment_ms=20 for sensitive clients. - There is a residual risk of increased token carryover memory in pathological long-prefix workloads; we cap automaton window to 32 tokens to bound memory.

review_comments: Marcus Chen: The automaton looks good; can we bound its memory overhead for long prefixes? Suggest cap=32 tokens — addressed in d90a4b5.
Owen Patel: Please add a regression test where a stop token is split across two fragments and a tool emits similar token bytes — added test_toolcall_stop_replay.py.
Lina Gomez: Will this affect non-streaming v1/chat.completions? — No, normalization runs for both but the demuxer only applies to streaming responses.
Security Review (SecurOps): Ensure toolcall sentinels cannot be injected by user content — we scoped sentinels to internal-only byte sequences and validated in framer.go.
Hannah Li (author): Responded to Marcus and Owen; added notes in docs about the cap and included microbenchmark results.
